name: Short 1 - touchscreen_first
script: Before the iPhone, Nokia engineers were already prototyping touchscreens. So in January 2007, when Steve Jobs walked out with the iPhone, Nokia's engineers weren't shocked by the hardware. They'd built touchscreens. What shocked them was the software. It felt like it belonged on a computer, not a phone. Nokia's phones ran Symbian, an operating system designed for buttons and tiny screens. And that's the part they couldn't copy fast enough.
